slides.title: Project Overview
points: Analyzes contact center transcripts to discover recurring business workflows automatically.
Combines large language models with clustering to produce structured process intelligence.
Targets operations teams, automation architects, and CX optimization stakeholders.
Converts raw interaction text into normalized task sequences and workflow clusters.
Supports process mining and orchestration design from real customer conversations.
Uses a configurable pipeline to adapt to domain-specific intent taxonomies.

slides.title: Business Problem
points: Operational workflow knowledge is buried in large volumes of unstructured call transcripts.
Manual analysis is expensive, inconsistent, and difficult to scale across intents.
Different agents describe similar actions using varied language and sequence patterns.
Without normalization, organizations cannot reliably identify repeatable process paths.
Process optimization efforts lack evidence from end-to-end customer interaction data.
Automation opportunities remain hidden without structured workflow discovery outputs.

slides.title: Solution Overview
points: Pipeline extracts workflow tasks from transcripts using intent-aware LLM prompts.
Task normalization clusters semantically similar actions into representative labels.
Sequence clustering groups complete workflow paths into common operational patterns.
Configuration-driven parameters control sampling, thresholds, and output destinations.
Outputs include Excel, JSON, and serialized artifacts for downstream analytics.
Design emphasizes privacy-aware extraction and deterministic processing controls.

slides.title: Detailed Step-Wise Execution Flow
points: Load intents and ranked interactions from structured metadata sources.
Sample transcripts by intent class to build representative processing batches.
Parse ASR rows into speaker-aware transcript narratives for model input.
Invoke LLM to infer workflow name, ordered tasks, and supporting analysis.
Generate embeddings for tasks and cluster them into normalized action groups.
Cluster normalized sequences and publish representative workflows with frequency counts.

slides.title: Core Capabilities & Architecture
points: Intent-guided extraction aligns detected workflows with business taxonomy context.
Semantic embedding and hierarchical clustering improve cross-phrase task consistency.
Representative task and workflow selection uses centroid-based nearest neighbor logic.
DBCV quality scoring supports evaluation of clustering density and separation.
Config manager centralizes paths, thresholds, model settings, and runtime parameters.
Model invocation layer standardizes Bedrock access, retries, and usage telemetry.

slides.title: Advantages
points: Reduces manual effort to discover workflows across large transcript corpora.
Creates standardized process language from heterogeneous agent conversation styles.
Improves visibility into frequent customer journey paths and operational bottlenecks.
Enables data-backed prioritization for automation and orchestration initiatives.
Supports repeatable experimentation through configurable thresholds and prompts.
Produces reusable structured outputs for analytics, governance, and reporting.

slides.title: Limitations
points: Extraction quality depends on transcript accuracy and intent metadata completeness.
LLM responses can vary when conversations are ambiguous or context is incomplete.
Clustering outcomes are sensitive to distance thresholds and embedding model choice.
Very large datasets may require batching to manage memory and runtime constraints.
Some nuanced tasks may be over-merged when semantic similarity is high.
Current implementation focuses on offline analysis rather than real-time streaming.

slides.title: Risks & Implementation Considerations
points: Cloud model availability and Bedrock rate limits influence throughput predictability.
Governance is required to monitor token cost and processing efficiency at scale.
Privacy controls must ensure sensitive details never leak into extracted outputs.
Quality thresholds should be validated per intent domain before operational rollout.
Fallback handling is needed for malformed model outputs or empty clusters.
Versioning of prompts and configs is essential for reproducible discovery results.

slides.title: Roadmap & Next Steps
points: Add interactive controls for threshold tuning and cluster quality exploration.
Integrate workflow title generation and richer taxonomy-aware labeling.
Expand evaluation framework with precision and recall benchmarks by intent.
Introduce human-in-the-loop review for low-confidence workflow inferences.
Enable incremental and near real-time processing for operational monitoring.
Package outputs for direct ingestion by orchestration and process mining platforms.
